summary: The connecting layer. It joins Slack, Linear, GitHub and the code into one graph: one Person per human across all tools, pending references that resolve when a source arrives, explicit and inferred mentions from any text to tickets, pull requests and code, the meaning layer (Feature, Decision, Procedure, KNOWS_ABOUT), and a thin record of each Actron request, its investigation and its build. Authoritative workflow state (ticket revisions, approvals, build logs) lives in the application database; the graph keeps what the agent needs to reason and remember. This file also defines the metadata every node and link carries, and node groups that relationships may use as their from_node or to_node; the loader expands a group into one relationship per member.
use_cases: Starting from a Slack request, what tickets, pull requests, decisions and functions are connected to it?
Which earlier decisions constrain the code this request would change, and where was each decided?
Who knows this function or feature best, across commits, reviews, tickets and Slack?
How are changes usually made in this part of the code (test command, files that change together)?
What did Actron find for this request, what did it hand to the builder, and what did the build produce?
Which references are still waiting for a source to be connected?

common_node_properties.name: source
common_node_properties.description: slack, linear, github, code, git or actron

common_node_properties.name: sourceUrl
common_node_properties.description: Link to the record in its tool, when one exists

common_node_properties.name: workspaceId
common_node_properties.description: Actron workspace (tenant) the node belongs to; one graph per workspace

common_node_properties.name: ontologyVersion
common_node_properties.description: Version of the ontology file that defined the node

common_node_properties.name: deleted
common_node_properties.description: Removed or no longer accessible in the source (tombstone)

common_relationship_properties.name: method
common_relationship_properties.description: explicit (an id or path written in the source), structural (from the API or parser), extracted (model read the text), inferred (model or heuristic judgement), confirmed (a person confirmed it)

common_relationship_properties.name: confidence
common_relationship_properties.description: 0 to 1. 1 for explicit and structural links; the model probability otherwise

common_relationship_properties.name: sourceRef
common_relationship_properties.description: Id of the node the link was derived from

common_relationship_properties.name: quote
common_relationship_properties.description: Exact supporting text, when the link came from text

common_relationship_properties.name: model
common_relationship_properties.description: Model and version for extracted or inferred links

common_relationship_properties.name: flag
common_relationship_properties.description: possible when a link check scored it between 0.5 and 0.7

common_relationship_properties.name: deleted
common_relationship_properties.description: Link no longer holds (its source was deleted, or the reference was edited out); kept for history and excluded from normal queries

common_relationship_properties.name: active
common_relationship_properties.description: CONSTRAINS only: false when a later decision superseded the constraint for this target while it stays in force for others

common_relationship_properties.name: supersededBy
common_relationship_properties.description: CONSTRAINS only: id of the decision that superseded this constraint for this target

action_classifications.description: Match Slack users, GitHub users, Linear users and git authors to one Person by email, then by an explicit mapping. Ambiguous matches stay unresolved.
Find ticket ids, PR and issue numbers, URLs, file paths and symbol names in text. Resolve them now or store a pending Reference.
Judge candidate links from text to features and code with a model; keep those above a threshold.
Create Decision nodes with the exact quote and their source; approved only with explicit evidence.
Verify each model-made link against its source text; flag or drop weak links.
Compute KNOWS_ABOUT from commits, blame, reviews, tickets and Slack participation.
Learn how changes are made in an area from merged pull requests and successful builds.
Write the thin Request, Investigation and BuildRun records and their links.

nodes.name: Workspace
nodes.label: Workspace
nodes.description: An Actron workspace (tenant). Each workspace has its own FalkorDB graph; this node is the root of that graph.

nodes.name: Identity
nodes.label: Identity
nodes.description: One account of a person in one tool, and how it was matched.

nodes.name: Team
nodes.label: Team
nodes.description: A group of people (from a Linear team or a Slack user group).

nodes.name: Reference
nodes.label: Reference
nodes.description: A reference found in text (ENG-17, #123, a URL, a path, a symbol). Resolved at once when the target exists, otherwise kept pending and resolved when that source is ingested.

properties.name: kind
properties.description: linear_issue, github_pr, github_issue, commit, file, symbol, slack_message (a Slack permalink or channel:ts), url

properties.name: key
properties.description: Normalised key used to find the target (ENG-17, owner/name#123, path, sha)

nodes.name: Feature
nodes.label: Feature
nodes.description: A named behaviour of the product (for example 'report export'), linked to the code that implements it and the text that discusses it.

nodes.name: Decision
nodes.label: Decision
nodes.description: A statement of how the software should or should not behave, with its exact source quote. Approved only with explicit evidence; otherwise proposed.

properties.name: statement
properties.description: The decision in one sentence (full-text indexed)

properties.name: status
properties.description: approved, proposed, superseded or rejected (rejected is set only when a later approved decision explicitly reverses this one without replacing it)

properties.name: quoteSpan
properties.description: [start, end] character offsets in the source text

properties.name: approvalEvidence
properties.description: Why it counts as approved (an explicit approval in the source), if it does

properties.name: confidence
properties.description: Model probability that this is a decision

properties.name: scope
properties.description: Where the decision applies, in plain words

properties.name: statementHistory
properties.description: Earlier statements when the source text was edited, oldest first

nodes.name: Procedure
nodes.label: Procedure
nodes.description: How changes are usually made in an area of the code: test command, files that change together, review norms. Learned from merged pull requests and successful builds, and reused by the next build.

properties.name: area
properties.description: Component or path prefix it applies to

properties.name: successCount
properties.description: Builds that followed it and passed

nodes.name: Request
nodes.label: Request
nodes.description: A feature request, bug report or question raised through Slack or the UI. Thin graph record; full workflow state is in the application database under the same id.

properties.name: state
properties.description: Mirror of the current workflow state

properties.name: outcome
properties.description: answered, merged, closed, cancelled, or empty while open

nodes.name: Investigation
nodes.label: Investigation
nodes.description: What the investigator agent found for a request: the evidence it handed to the builder.

nodes.name: BuildRun
nodes.label: BuildRun
nodes.description: One run of the coding agent for an approved request.
